title: Registration, Proof of Residency and Required Documents
content:
## Rule

1. Under Student Enrollment, Transfers and Pre-Kindergarten Admissions, a new registration starts in status provisional, and the student attends from the entry date.
2. For an enrollment type whose in-district residence requirement applies, a student is registered only when the household profile shows an in-district residence. The district's household record decides; what the family says does not replace it.
3. A provisional registration becomes enrolled only once the documents the type requires are on file for that enrollment: a proof of residency whose document date is no more than 60 days before its received date, when the type requires a residency proof, and a birth certificate for a student who is new to the district. The documents are those the registrar has logged as received on that enrollment. The registrar verifies them, and on verification the registration becomes a full enrollment; the date residency was verified is recorded, and left empty when the type requires no residency proof.
4. When residency is not established within the type's residency deadline (calendar days after the registration date, the registration date being day 0), the registration is withdrawn with the leaver reason "residency not established". The withdrawal date is the last day of attendance, and the student's School Nutrition Services Meal Account becomes inactive on that date.
5. A missing birth certificate after the type's birth certificate deadline (calendar days from the entry date) is referred to local law enforcement as Texas Education Code 25.002 requires, and it does not end the enrollment. A student transferring from another Texas public school may attend for the type's provisional immunization period (calendar days) while immunization records are obtained.
6. When the type re-verifies residency every school year, a returning-student registration needs a new proof of residency for the new school year.

Which types require residency and a residency proof, and the length of each deadline, are set per enrollment type in the registrar's schedule of registration documents and in the enrollment type schedule.

## The 60-day age of a residency proof (hypothetical dates)

The document date is compared with the date the registrar accepted the document:
- document dated 10 January, received 11 March of a non-leap year: 60 days before the received date, so the proof qualifies;
- the same document received 12 March: 61 days, so it does not qualify;
- document dated the same day it was received: 0 days, so it qualifies.

## What moves a provisional registration

| Situation on the enrollment | Result |
|---|---|
| The required residency proof (if the type requires one) and, for a new-to-district student, a birth certificate are on file | becomes enrolled on verification |
| A required document is missing | stays provisional |
| Residency not established by the residency deadline | withdrawn, leaver reason "residency not established" |
| Birth certificate missing after its deadline | referred to local law enforcement; the enrollment continues |
